prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer up front: there’s no single “best” course — the right program depends on whether you want Jungian/depth-psychology shadow work, somatic/trauma‑informed integration, or spiritual/meditative practice. Below are reputable, well‑reviewed online options grouped by approach, plus beginner resources, safety guidance, and how to choose.

Recommended Jungian / depth-psychology shadow-work
- Jung Platform (subscription and single courses)
  - Focus: Jungian shadow, dreams, archetypes, active imagination.
  - Who it’s good for: people wanting classic depth‑psychology frameworks and practical rituals.
  - Format: short courses, workshops, video lessons and Q&A.
- Depth Psychology Alliance
  - Focus: lectures and courses from contemporary Jungian analysts and depth psychologists.
  - Who it’s good for: learners wanting ongoing deep study and community.
  - Format: membership with live events, courses, recordings.

Recommended trauma‑informed / somatic integration (if you have trauma)
- Somatic Experiencing (SE) and Sensorimotor Psychotherapy (trainings)
  - Focus: body‑based stabilization, nervous system regulation, and integration of difficult material.
  - Who it’s good for: people with trauma histories or those who notice strong somatic reactions during inner work.
  - Format: professional trainings are long, but both organizations offer introductory online workshops and practitioner directories.
- Course-style programs by trauma‑informed therapists (search for “trauma‑informed shadow work” + therapist name)
  - Look for therapists who explicitly integrate somatics and safety practices.

Recommended meditation & contemplative/spiritual practice
- Tara Brach (courses/retreats; many offerings on Sounds True and her site)
  - Focus: mindfulness, radical acceptance, compassion — excellent for emotional regulation and inner observation.
- Jack Kornfield / Spirit Rock / Insight Meditation Society (IMS)
  - Focus: Buddhist meditation, ethical framework, retreats/teacher trainings.
- Sounds True
  - Focus: many high‑quality courses on both shadow topics (e.g., Debbie Ford material) and spiritual practice (Tara Brach, Jack Kornfield, Pema Chödrön audio/video teachings).

Popular course marketplaces / apps (mixed quality — vet instructors)
- Insight Timer — thousands of free/low‑cost guided meditations and multi‑week courses on inner child/shadow themes.
- Udemy — plenty of “shadow work” courses; read reviews and instructor credentials carefully.
- Mindvalley — pop‑spirituality courses that incorporate shadow/inner work (good for motivational, community formats; less depth than clinical/Jungian options).
- Gaia — documentary and course content on myth, archetype, shadow; more “esoteric.”

Books & short structured programs to use alongside courses
- Owning Your Own Shadow by Robert A. Johnson (short, clear introduction)
- Meeting the Shadow (edited anthology)
- The Dark Side of the Light Chasers by Debbie Ford (practical exercises)
- Radical Acceptance by Tara Brach; When Things Fall Apart by Pema Chödrön — for spiritual grounding

How to choose the best course for you
- Clarify your aim: psychological integration (Jung/psychotherapy), trauma healing (somatic/therapist), or spiritual awakening (meditation/nondual).
- Instructor credibility: look for clinicians, Jungian analysts, long‑time meditation teachers, or trauma specialists when dealing with heavy material.
- Format preference: self‑paced videos, live group, small cohort with coaching, or long retreat.
- Reviews and preview content: watch sample lessons and read reviews; see if there’s a refund policy.

Safety & practice guidelines (important)
- Shadow work often surfaces intense emotions and memories. If you have a history of complex trauma, severe depression, suicidality, or dissociation, do not attempt deep shadow work alone — work with a licensed therapist or trauma‑informed practitioner.
- Favor courses that teach stabilization skills (grounding, breath techniques, somatic resourcing) before deep excavation.
- Start small: 10–20 minute journaling + guided meditation sessions; limit very deep sessions and integrate with grounding afterward.
- Keep a support plan: trusted friend, therapist, crisis contacts.

Suggested beginner pathway (practical)
1. Read one short book (Robert Johnson or Debbie Ford) to learn basic concepts.
2. Start a short meditation course (Tara Brach or IMS/Spirit Rock intro) to build stability.
3. Take a structured introductory shadow course (Jung Platform or a well‑reviewed Udemy/Sounds True course).
4. If deeper material arises, add somatic learning or see a trauma‑informed therapist.

If you want, tell me:
- Which approach appeals most (Jungian, somatic/trauma, Buddhist/meditation, spiritual/new‑age)?
- Any history of trauma or current mental‑health concerns?

I can then give 3–5 specific course recommendations tailored to your goals and budget.
